title: Meridian Grid Labs and Halcyon Quantum Start Contingency Analysis Pilot for Midwestern Utilities
snippet: DENVER and CHICAGO, Aug. 10, 2026 — Meridian Grid Labs and Halcyon Quantum today started a contingency analysis pilot for three Midwestern transmission utilities.
articleText: DENVER and CHICAGO, Aug. 10, 2026 — Meridian Grid Labs, a transmission analytics company, and Halcyon Quantum, a neutral-atom quantum computing developer, today started a contingency analysis pilot for three Midwestern transmission utilities. The pilot applies Halcyon Quantum Orion Series processors to N-1 and N-2 contingency screening for a 4,200-bus planning model supplied by the utilities. Meridian Grid Labs Contingency Engine Version 4 will run the classical baseline and compare solve times, screening coverage, and ranking stability against the quantum-assisted workflow. The utilities asked for results on the winter 2026 peak case, the summer 2027 peak case, and a data center interconnection case that adds 900 megawatts of new load across two substations. Halcyon Quantum Chief Technology Officer Dana Reyes said the processors will run the screening on a 256-atom register with error mitigation applied in software. Meridian Grid Labs Chief Executive Officer Priya Natarajan said the comparison will decide whether the utilities keep the quantum-assisted workflow in their 2027 planning cycle. Argonne National Laboratory Grid Analytics Group researchers will review the methodology and publish an independent assessment in the first quarter of 2027. Midcontinent Independent System Operator planners will receive the screening results but are not a party to the agreement. Halcyon Quantum will host the processors in its Boulder facility and the utilities will transfer planning models under a data handling agreement signed in July. The companies expect the first comparison report in December 2026 and a decision on a multi-year contract by March 2027. Capacity for the pilot is reserved on two processors, and Halcyon Quantum said additional utilities can join the program after the first report is published.
